tasks.goal: a Node CLI 'inicheck' that validates INI files: reads a path as argv[2], prints 'OK <n> sections' to stdout when every line is a [section], key=value, comment (;) or blank, exits 1 with a clear stderr error naming the first offending line otherwise or when the file is missing. Ship package.json, a fixtures/ dir with one valid and one invalid sample, and a README with a 'Verified invocations' section. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, re-verify the finished deliverable: re-run every invocation documented in the README exactly as written and confirm stdout/stderr/exit codes match what the README claims.

a Node CLI 'jsonpick' that extracts a value from a JSON file: reads a path as argv[2] and a dot-path as argv[3] (e.g. a.b.0.c), prints the value as JSON to stdout, exits 1 with a clear stderr error on a missing file, invalid JSON, or an unresolvable path. Ship package.json, a fixtures/ dir with a nested sample, and a README with a 'Verified invocations' section. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, re-verify the finished deliverable: re-run every invocation documented in the README exactly as written and confirm stdout/stderr/exit codes match what the README claims.

a single-file index.html click-counter widget: a large count display starting at 0, increment and decrement buttons, a reset button, and the count turning red when negative. No external assets. Serve it with a local static server and verify in a real browser that the page loads with zero console errors and the buttons actually change the displayed count.

a single-file index.html stopwatch web app: start/stop/lap buttons, elapsed time display with centiseconds, and a lap list. No external assets. Serve it with a local static server and verify in a real browser that the page loads with zero console errors, the display advances after Start is clicked, and Lap appends an entry.

a zero-dependency Node HTTP JSON API 'kvstore': PUT /kv/<key> stores the raw JSON body under the key and returns 204; GET /kv/<key> returns the stored JSON or 404; DELETE /kv/<key> removes it (204 or 404); GET /kv lists all keys as a JSON array. Items live in memory. Start the server and verify EVERY endpoint including the error cases with real HTTP requests, reporting the observed status codes and bodies.

a zero-dependency Node HTTP service 'pinger' with two endpoints: GET /healthz returns 200 {"ok":true,"uptimeMs":<number>} and GET /echo?msg=<text> returns 200 {"echo":"<text>"} or 400 with a JSON error when msg is missing. Start the server and verify both endpoints including the error case with real HTTP requests, reporting the observed status codes and bodies.
